finding.expected: Keep the bounded provenance gate and all accepted/rejected actor semantics, but reuse existing canonical PRE_AIOS reason codes already admitted by Operational Receipt v2 instead of creating new taxonomy. Use an existing authorization/input reason such as UNAUTHORIZED_DELIVERY_ACTOR for unauthorized provenance and INVALID_BOUNDED_INPUT for invalid executor/selector binding as appropriate. Add a deterministic regression in the authorized workflow test file proving every reason_code emitted by the modified provenance gate belongs to the existing repository-owned WORKFLOW_REASONS set. Do not modify src/aios_renew/operational_receipt.py, widen TASK-160 scope, weaken the bot empty-executor/exact-ID constraints, or change Runtime/REPAIR semantics.
finding.issue: The candidate introduces three new inline PRE_AIOS reason_code values (UNAUTHORIZED_DELIVERY_EVENT, UNAUTHORIZED_AUTOMATION_EXECUTOR, and REPAIR_DISPATCH_ID_MISMATCH), but the canonical Operational Receipt v2 WORKFLOW_REASONS taxonomy in src/aios_renew/operational_receipt.py does not recognize them. TASK-160 explicitly requires preserving Operational Receipt v2 and does not authorize changing that schema/taxonomy. The workflow can therefore emit WORKFLOW-owned receipts that the repository-owned operational receipt contract itself would reject, creating two inconsistent reason vocabularies for the same boundary.
